form_descriptions.address: Refers to some location in the address space of the described program.
form_descriptions.block: An arbitrary number of uninterpreted bytes of data.
form_descriptions.constant: One, two, four or eight bytes of uninterpreted data, or data encoded in the variable length format known as LEB128 (see Section 7.6.). Most constant values are integers of one kind or another (codes, offsets, counts, and so on); these are sometimes called “integer constants” for emphasis.
form_descriptions.flag: A small constant that indicates the presence or absence of an attribute.
form_descriptions.lineptr: Refers to a location in the DWARF section that holds line number information.
form_descriptions.loclistptr: Refers to a location in the DWARF section that holds location lists, which describe objects whose location can change during their lifetime.
form_descriptions.macptr: Refers to a location in the DWARF section that holds macro definition information.
form_descriptions.rangelistptr: Refers to a location in the DWARF section that holds non-contiguous address ranges.
form_descriptions.reference: Refers to one of the debugging information entries that describe the program. There are two types of reference. The first is an offset relative to the beginning of the compilation unit in which the reference occurs and must refer to an entry within that same compilation unit. The second type of reference is the offset of a debugging information entry in any compilation unit, including one different from the unit containing the reference.
form_descriptions.string: A null-terminated sequence of zero or more (non-null) bytes. Data in this form are generally printable strings. Strings may be represented directly in the debugging information entry or as an offset in a separate string table.

form_descriptions.address: Refers to some location in the address space of the described program.
form_descriptions.block: An arbitrary number of uninterpreted bytes of data.
form_descriptions.constant: One, two, four or eight bytes of uninterpreted data, or data encoded in the variable length format known as LEB128 (see Section 7.6.). Most constant values are integers of one kind or another (codes, offsets, counts, and so on); these are sometimes called “integer constants” for emphasis.
form_descriptions.exprloc: A DWARF expression or location description.
form_descriptions.flag: A small constant that indicates the presence or absence of an attribute.
form_descriptions.lineptr: Refers to a location in the DWARF section that holds line number information.
form_descriptions.loclistptr: Refers to a location in the DWARF section that holds location lists, which describe objects whose location can change during their lifetime.
form_descriptions.macptr: Refers to a location in the DWARF section that holds macro definition information.
form_descriptions.rangelistptr: Refers to a location in the DWARF section that holds non-contiguous address ranges.
form_descriptions.reference: Refers to one of the debugging information entries that describe the program. There are three types of reference. The first is an offset relative to the beginning of the compilation unit in which the reference occurs and must refer to an entry within that same compilation unit. The second type of reference is the offset of a debugging information entry in any compilation unit, including one different from the unit containing the reference. The third type of reference is an indirect reference to a type definition using a 64-bit signature for that type.
form_descriptions.string: A null-terminated sequence of zero or more (non-null) bytes. Data in this class are generally printable strings. Strings may be represented directly in the debugging information entry or as an offset in a separate string table.
